question: Which OCR runtime (llama.cpp GGUF, MLX or the shipped backend) can serve each engine, without losing output quality?
decision: Whether either engine gets a follow-up OpenSpec change for a llama.cpp path, and which GGUF arm that change uses.

hypotheses.statement: At least one of the two scored llama.cpp GGUF arms (D4 for dots.mocr, P4 for PaddleOCR-VL) meets gates C1 to C5 against its engine's shipped backend.
hypotheses.null: Neither D4 nor P4 meets all of C1 to C5 against the shipped backend of its engine.

decision_rule: Each engine has one scored GGUF arm: D4 for dots.mocr, P4 for PaddleOCR-VL. If that arm passes C1 to C5, open a follow-up OpenSpec change for a llama.cpp path for that arm. If it fails, the engine keeps its shipped backend. MLX arms never lead to an engine decision. If an MLX arm passes and the GGUF arm of its engine does not, report that and stop.
baseline: shipped backends: dots.mocr on PyTorch MPS (D0), PaddleOCR-VL on CPU (P0)
candidate: Scored GGUF arms D4 and P4 (decide); scored MLX 8-bit arms D2 and P2 (comparison only). D1, D3, P1 and P3 are conditional 16-bit diagnostics that never change a verdict.

comparisons.matched_runtime_caveat: D4 against D2 is not precision-matched. GGUF Q8_0 quantises linear tensors in blocks of 32 elements with a symmetric scale, and the mmproj stays 16-bit. MLX 8-bit uses affine quantisation with group size 64 (config.json of mlx-community/dots.mocr-8bit at 6d9e750b: bits 8, group_size 64, mode affine; read via the HF API on 2026-10-30). In that build the vision tower is not quantised: model.safetensors.index.json lists no .scales entry for its 304 vision tensors. OpenGryd/PaddleOCR-VL-1.6-MLX-8bit at dba7c66b uses the same settings and has 84 scale tensors among its 503 vision-named tensors, so part of its vision stack is quantised. The comparison is reported only. The two pairs also differ in image format: PaddleX sends PNG blocks to llama-cpp-server and JPEG blocks to mlx-vlm-server (paddlex doc_vlm/predictor.py line 595), so P2 receives JPEG blocks and P4 receives PNG.

preprocessing_parity.why: The runtime must be the only variable. Each runtime resizes the page image in its own way. The image token flags come from the processor configs and are pinned before the plan freeze. The parity check on the smoke pages (protocol procedure step 8) confirms them.

baseline_dots_mocr.render: pypdfium2 at 200 DPI. The scale is raised so the long side is at least 1600 px: scale = max(200/72, 1600/max(page size in points)). Source: ocr-workers/engines/dots-mocr/src/omrs_ocr_dots_mocr/engine.py lines 40-41 (RENDER_DPI, MIN_LONG_SIDE_PX) and line 126.
baseline_dots_mocr.resize: qwen_vl_utils.process_vision_info (engine.py line 143), then the HF processor (engine.py line 144). The engine passes no min_pixels or max_pixels to process_vision_info. qwen_vl_utils sets IMAGE_MIN_TOKEN_NUM 4 and IMAGE_MAX_TOKEN_NUM 16384 (qwen_vl_utils/vision_process.py lines 26-27, installed in the engine environment). The processor file preprocessor_config.json in the model folder sets min_pixels 3136, max_pixels 11,289,600, patch_size 14 and merge_size 2. One image token covers 28 x 28 = 784 px. In tokens, the minimum is 4 (3136 px) and the maximum is 14,400 (11,289,600 px).
baseline_dots_mocr.baseline_token_count: Computed without a model run: pass the rendered image through the HF processor and read image_grid_thw. The token count is the grid product divided by 4.

preprocessing_parity.baseline_paddleocr_vl: The P0 pipeline resizes each layout block crop to min_pixels 112,896 and max_pixels 1,003,520 (paddlex/inference/pipelines/paddleocr_vl/pipeline.py lines 663-666, paddlex 3.7.2). In tokens of 784 px, the minimum is 144 and the maximum is 1280. For llama-cpp-server and mlx-vlm-server, PaddleX does not apply these limits. It only warns that the backend does not support max_pixels (paddlex/inference/models/doc_vlm/predictor.py lines 536-560) and sends the raw crop. The backend must therefore match the P0 limits itself.
preprocessing_parity.llama_cpp: llama.cpp resizes through the server flags --image-min-tokens and --image-max-tokens (and the mmproj default clip.vision.image_max_pixels). The official PaddleOCR-VL-1.6 mmproj default is 1,003,520 pixels (PaddlePaddle/PaddleOCR-VL-1.6-GGUF README at 511b0964), equal to the P0 upper limit. For the dots.mocr mmproj of our own conversion, read the default from the file metadata and record it. The flags set the limits, so no mmproj file needs an edit.
preprocessing_parity.mlx: mlx-vlm resizes through its own processor. D2: min_pixels 3136 and max_pixels 11,289,600 from the model's preprocessor_config.json. P2: min_pixels 112,896 and max_pixels 1,003,520. Confirm at the parity check that mlx-vlm applies them.

rule.where: The parity check runs on the smoke pages (eq01 p2 and p3) for each 8-bit arm, in protocol procedure step 8, before the plan freeze. It checks token grids only and scores nothing.
rule.d_arms: Compare the resized grid with image_grid_thw of the baseline. At most one patch row or one patch column of difference is allowed.
rule.p_arms: Apply the same test per layout block. The baseline grid for a block comes from the P0 resize rule on the same crop. No model run is needed.
rule.on_failure: If a grid differs by more, stop that arm and fix the setting before the freeze. If build 11941 ignores --image-min-tokens or --image-max-tokens, stop that arm and record a finding (OI-10). Do not loosen the tolerance.

D_arms.rule: A page hits the cap when completion_tokens >= 8192. That page yields an empty result. MLX uses its generated token count for the same test.
D_arms.baseline_source: ocr-workers/engines/dots-mocr/src/omrs_ocr_dots_mocr/engine.py line 111 passes hit_token_cap=new_tokens >= MAX_NEW_TOKENS (MAX_NEW_TOKENS = 8192, line 42). layout.py lines 114-115: page_markdown returns "" with reason token_cap.

P_arms.cap: The P0 cap is 4096 tokens per block request, not 8192.
P_arms.evidence: paddleocr-vl engine.py line 132 calls pipeline.predict(input=...) with no max_new_tokens. paddlex pipeline.py lines 966-972 pass "max_new_tokens": None in vlm_kwargs, and lines 504-505 set it to 4096. The 8192 default (doc_vlm/predictor.py lines 229-232 and 513-516) is never reached. PaddleOCR-VL-1.6.yaml has no override. Experiment 37 used paddleocr 3.7.0 and paddlex 3.7.2, the same versions as the engine lock.
P_arms.rule: P arms pass max_new_tokens=4096. P0's reused output keeps truncated block text, and a P arm keeps truncated text in the same way. Each block with completion_tokens >= 4096 is logged as a cap hit. The log is information only. A cap hit does not empty the page.

conditional_diagnostic.why: An 8-bit arm differs from its baseline in runtime and in weight precision. The diagnostic separates the two causes of a quality failure.
conditional_diagnostic.trigger: an 8-bit arm fails C3, C4 or C5 (C1 and C2 do not trigger it)
conditional_diagnostic.arm: the 16-bit arm of the same runtime and engine (diagnostic_for)

pages.C3: the 68 pages of E-maths and E-scan
pages.C5: the pages of the failed arm's review list

conditional_diagnostic.scored: the failed gate only, on those pages
conditional_diagnostic.reading: 16-bit passes the pass_rule on the failed gate's pages: 8-bit quantisation caused the failure. 16-bit does not: the runtime caused it. The attribution is approximate. Every GGUF arm keeps a 16-bit mmproj, while MLX 8-bit quantises different tensors (the language model; for dots.mocr 8-bit the vision tower is not quantised), so the diagnostic cannot isolate one factor.
conditional_diagnostic.limits: Descriptive only. Never changes the verdict of the 8-bit arm. A 16-bit pass supports at most a separate follow-up experiment on all 257 pages.
conditional_diagnostic.cost: none when no 8-bit arm fails; otherwise D1 6.1 GB or P1 1.8 GB download (D3 and P3 exist locally) and about 20 to 60 minutes per triggered arm
conditional_diagnostic.pass_rule: The threshold is the failed gate's own tolerance, applied to the baseline arm's value on the same pages. C3: the baseline KaTeX error rate on the 68 pages of E-maths and E-scan plus 0.01 (absolute). C4: the baseline median recall on the same 40 seeded E-script pages minus 0.05. C5: the operator reviews the diagnostic output on the same review pages and finds no invented text.
